name: rp
desc: Tool to find ROP sequences in PE/Elf/Mach-O x86/x64 binaries
why: Finds ROP gadgets in binaries, a direct window into how exploits chain code fragments together.

brief.what_it_is: rp++ (invoked as rp) is a C++ command-line tool that searches compiled executables for ROP gadgets, which are short instruction sequences ending in a return that exploit chains can reuse. It takes a PE, ELF, or Mach-O binary (or a raw code dump with --raw) and an instruction-count limit given with --rop, and prints the gadgets it finds. It also searches a binary for pointers to specific integer values (--search-int) or byte strings (--search-hexa), which are useful when assembling a ROP chain. The README describes it as supporting x86, x64, ARM, and ARM64 architectures.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames it as a helper for building ROP chains: when constructing one, you often need gadgets and also pointers to integers or strings with specific values. The author describes it as a fast gadget finder.
brief.how_it_works: You point it at a file with --file or -f and set the maximum number of instructions per gadget with --rop or -r. --va sets the module base address (passing 0 gives relative offsets), and --raw analyses raw code dumps instead of parsed executables. The README does not describe the internal scanning algorithm.

commands_seen.context: Build-from-source example for Linux, run from the src/build directory; the README says each supported platform has its own build script there. The sample output shows GCC 9.3.0 and a final link step producing rp-lin-x64.

brief.install_notes: The README only documents building from source with the shell scripts in src/build, and the Linux example shows a CMake-style configure and a C++ compiler (GCC 9.3.0 in the sample output). The Homebrew formula installs an executable named rp-osx. The README says nothing about runtime dependencies, accounts, or configuration.
brief.standout: Unlike a plain gadget lister, it also searches for pointers to specific integer values and strings, which covers the other half of building a ROP chain. The README shows animated GIFs of each mode.
brief.status: unknown. The README has a Builds CI badge and no release dates or changelog. I did not check the commit history or releases page, so I cannot give a last-commit date.
brief.caveats: The README gives no explicit license. The Homebrew description lists only x86/x64, while the README also claims ARM and ARM64, so support for the newer architectures may be uneven. The build examples are Linux-oriented, and the Homebrew package is named rp-osx. The README includes no usage examples beyond the GIFs and option descriptions. The scout note's framing about exploits is not in the README.
quotes: rp++ or rp is a C++ ROP gadget finder for PE/ELF/Mach-O executables and x86/x64/ARM/ARM64 architectures.
To find ROP gadget you need to specify a file with the --file / -f option and use the --rop / -r option specifying the maximum the number of instructions in the gadget
Oftentimes when building ROP chains, you might need to find pointers to integers with specific values.
